title: What can people and AI accomplish together? — question tree
original_curiosity: Understand the full landscape of human–AI intellectual collaboration, from everyday use to extraordinary research, and develop the constituent capabilities.
parent_purpose: Increase independent human capacity to investigate, build, discover and verify ambitious things with AI.
framing: Achievements and transferable collaboration capabilities are distinct axes. Relative percentile labels are only metaphors unless grounded in representative population data.

nodes.question: What can people and AI accomplish together, and how could I get exceptionally good at it?
nodes.why_ask: Start with the curiosity, not a purported ranking or a prescribed workflow.

nodes.question: What are people actually accomplishing with AI?
nodes.why_ask: Discover the possibility landscape without equating publicity with evidence.

nodes.why_ask: Prioritize capabilities with reach, not a checklist of platform tricks.

nodes.question: Can I recognize and ask questions that matter before solving them?
nodes.why_ask: Test problem framing and question-navigation independently of answer generation.

nodes.question: When does more parallel AI work help, and when does it create coordination overhead?
nodes.why_ask: Investigate interfaces, independence and quality control.

nodes.question: Can an AI help improve how we investigate, not just answer the current question?
nodes.why_ask: Explore self-revision of representations, tests, and question selection.

nodes.question: How would we know that AI actually made us better?
nodes.why_ask: Avoid equating speed, subjective fluency or volume of output with capability.

candidate_references.role: Suggested first-hand resource; interpretation and limitations to investigate

nodes.question: Could I do the same work more reliably without AI?
nodes.why_ask: Make counterfactual comparisons across representative tasks.

candidate_references.role: Suggested first-hand resource; interpretation and limitations to investigate

nodes.question: Am I getting better at the task, or only better at operating a particular tool?
nodes.why_ask: Test competence after tool removal and transfer to new contexts.

nodes.question: Which outcomes matter: time, novelty, accuracy, understanding, cost, or reuse?
nodes.why_ask: Do not compress incomparable dimensions into a single fake percentile.

nodes.question: What would it take to go beyond the best examples we can currently find?
nodes.why_ask: Seek new compositions, bottleneck removals, and better questions.

nodes.question: What are the present obstructions: knowledge, verification, autonomy, tools, or cost?
nodes.why_ask: Determine what new capability would most expand the reachable set.

nodes.question: Could the best next step be to invent a better test or discover a different problem?
nodes.why_ask: Treat the investigation itself as a system we can improve.

connections.why: A claimed result and measured increase in capability are different things
Expertise may be the prerequisite rather than a replaceable prompt
Tool and evaluator architecture can multiply model ability
The evaluator defines which improvements are detectable
Improved investigative capability can accelerate acquisition of further capabilities

possible_perspectives: Achievement: what was produced and how strongly was it verified
Practice: what the human and AI each did
Transfer: what a nonexpert or another expert could reproduce
Economics: time, cost, attention and reliability
Generativity: which capabilities improve the next investigation
selection_rule: Expand branches only where plausible answers would change what to learn, compare or build; never manufacture an exhaustive tier ladder.
guidance: Use ordinary, curious questions first (RSM-01.03). Branch into possible answers and their consequences (RSM-02.08). Keep candidate evidence separate from established conclusions (RSM-01.04). Distinguish question trees from investigation trees (RSM-05).
